title: Micro-OPS SDK checklist and annotated quickstart (sketch)
content:
Overview:

This is a compact, operational-first sketch for a tiny SDK quickstart and an accompanying checklist intended for rapid adoption by internal integrators and early external pilot customers. The focus is: minimal cognitive load, built-in telemetry for safety/observability, and a clear path from zero-to-instrumented-hello-world in under 12 minutes.

Why Micro-OPS?
- Many existing quickstarts assume a full-featured demo app. Micro-OPS is intentionally small: ship one reliable call, capture useful telemetry, and show failure modes + recovery paths.
- Targets teams who need to embed Redwood inference into production flows (chat, embed, rerank) and want to validate latency/cost quickly without heavy integration.

Goals (measurable):
- Time-to-first-successful-inference <= 12 minutes for a competent engineer following the quickstart.
- Instrumentation: token-level latency and model-selection tag emitted on first request.
- Error surface documented: 6 common failure signatures with one-liner remediations.
- Usability score >= 4/5 from 5 pilot integrators in internal trial.

Audience:
- Primary: Platform/feature engineers integrating client-side SDKs in web/mobile backend services.
- Secondary: Solutions engineers running pilots for customers, SDK docs writers.

Constraints and assumptions:
- Minimal external dependencies (one HTTP client, one logging lib).
- Works in hosted Redwood API and Dedicated; Private requires minor network instructions.
- No heavy runtime (no sidecars, no local model runtime).

Non-goals:
- This is NOT a full reference; it intentionally omits advanced features (batching strategies, fine-grained caching, quantization profiles). Those live in separate deep-dive docs.

Success metrics (post-pilot):
- 10 pilot integrations complete within 2 weeks of doc publication.
- Median first-request latency observed by pilots < 90 ms (edge regions).
- Pilot telemetry emitted and surfaced in Console dashboards for all 10 pilots.

Deliverables (MVP):
- Annotated Quickstart doc (this sketch -> polished text + screenshots).
- Tiny example repo: /examples/microops (Node + Python minimal handlers).
- Checklist: 1-page ops checklist for SEs and integrators.
- Telemetry contract: minimal events and schema for Console ingestion.

High-level rollout timeline (4 sprints):
- Sprint 0 (planning, this doc): alignment with SRE and Console teams (1 week).
- Sprint 1 (quickstart + Node example, 1 week): publish draft, internal trial.
- Sprint 2 (Python example + telemetry hooks, 1 week): expand examples and add error-mode guidance.
- Sprint 3 (cleanup + pilot support, 1 week): incorporate feedback, finalize acceptance criteria.

Annotated Quickstart (core flow)
- Objective: Call Redwood API to get a short chat/generation output, record minimal telemetry, demonstrate fallback when model unavailable.
- Estimated follow time: 10–12 minutes.

Pre-reqs:
- Redwood API key (free trial or demo org).
- Node 18+ (or Python 3.10+).
- Small text editor and terminal.

1) Create project and install tiny client
- Node: npm init -y && npm i node-fetch tiny-log
- Python: python -m venv venv && pip install requests structlog

Notes: we intentionally avoid heavy Redwood SDK wrappers in the MVP so users see raw interactions; later we ship the ergonomic wrapper.

2) Minimal request (annotated)
- Purpose: show the absolute minimum HTTP payload and response fields we rely on.
- Node pseudo:
  const fetch = require('node-fetch')
  const API_KEY = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'rw-bison-1', prompt: 'Summarize: The quickstart is tiny.' })
  })
  const json = await res.json()
  console.log(json.output_text)

- Python pseudo:
  import os, requests
  API_KEY = os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')
  r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {API_KEY}'}, json={'model':'rw-bison-1','prompt':'Summarize: The quickstart is tiny.'})
  print(r.json().get('output_text'))

3) Annotated telemetry hook (minimal events)
- Emit event: inference.request.start with tags: model, route, client_lang.
- Emit event: inference.request.done with tags: model, latency_ms, status_code, selected_variant.
- Storage: send to Console via a single POST to /ingest/telemetry (or rely on SDK wrapper later).

Why in quickstart: seeing telemetry emitted on first request is a strong trust signal for SEs and SREs.

4) Fallback demo (network/model fail)
- Simulate by swapping model name to model-not-found or by returning 503.
- Quick remediation steps in the doc: check API key scopes, check model compatibility table, switch to a lower-capacity variant (rw-bison-lite) and re-run.

5) Sanity checks and acceptance
- Console: check that an inference.request.done event shows latency and model tag.
- Local: confirm printed output_text and exit code 0.

Ops checklist (one pager):
- [ ] API key created and exported as env var
- [ ] Minimal request returns 200 with output_text in payload
- [ ] Telemetry events appear in Console within 60s
- [ ] Error cases reproduced and quick fixes applied
- [ ] Latency and token cost recorded in pilot notes

Telemetry contract (MVP fields):
- event: inference.request.start -> { timestamp, trace_id, client_lang, model_name, route }
- event: inference.request.done -> { timestamp, trace_id, latency_ms, status, model_variant, input_token_count, output_token_count }

Instrumenting for cost-awareness (quick tip):
- Surface tokens in the first request so integrators can estimate per-request cost. Add a one-line helper that logs tokens and estimated $/req assuming published pricing.

Ergonomics decisions (short notes):
- Keep payload small; avoid open-ended streaming in the first pass.
- Prefer JSON with stable fields (output_text, metadata) rather than vendor-specific nested objects.
- Provide a single function example in the later ergonomic wrapper: redwood.generate(prompt, opts) -> { text, tokens, latency }

Common failure signatures (6) and one-line fixes:
1) 401 Unauthorized -> check REDWOOD_API_KEY env var and scopes.
2) 404 Model Not Found -> consult model catalog, pick compatible variant.
3) 429 Rate Limit -> reduce client concurrency or request a quota bump (link to ticket template).
4) 503 Service Unavailable -> retry with exponential backoff; check status.dashboard for incidents.
5) Large prompt truncation -> validate token counts against model max; surface error.
6) Telemetry not visible -> ensure ingest key present and verify ingest endpoint.

Acceptance criteria (MVP ready):
- Quickstart doc published in Drive and linked from SDK landing.
- Example repo builds and runs: Node + Python verified by CI smoke test.
- Telemetry events pass schema validation in Console test harness.
- 5 internal SEs try it and file no more than 3 actionable UX bugs.

Open questions and proposals:
- Do we include a minimal streaming snippet for chat within the first pass, or wait until ergonomics wrapper is ready? Proposal: delay streaming until wrapper exists to avoid coupling.
- Should we surface cost-estimate badges in example README? Proposal: yes, but opt-in and calculated from pilot pricing tiers.

Next steps (short):
- Rafael: scaffold example repo and basic CI (1 week).
- Devon: wire telemetry contract into Console ingest sandbox (1 week).
- Priya: draft polished prose and screenshots for the quickstart (3 days).
- Samantha (owner): run internal 10-person pilot and collect feedback (2 weeks).

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep language low friction; call out "do this first" and "if this fails" blocks clearly.
- Use very small code examples; real SDK calls will be developed in parallel.
- Link to model catalog and latency benchmarks in final doc.

Contact and support: reach out to #devexp on Slack or ping the owner (Samantha Park) for pilot coordination.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-04: initial sketch and outline created.
- 2026-01-15: added telemetry contract and fallback checklist after sync with Console team.
- 2026-02-28: incorporated early internal feedback; updated acceptance criteria and timeline.
